title: Portolá Sights the Bay
description: Gaspar de Portolá's overland expedition views San Francisco Bay from Sweeney Ridge; Sgt. José Ortega's scouts had first seen it on November 1.

title: Through the Golden Gate
description: Juan Manuel de Ayala's San Carlos passes through the Golden Gate; its crew are the first Europeans known to enter the bay, staying until September 18.

title: Presidio Founded
description: Spain establishes the Presidio of San Francisco, the northernmost outpost of New Spain, to guard the bay.

title: Mission Dolores
description: Frs. Francisco Palóu and Pedro Benito Cambón dedicate Mission San Francisco de Asís; its adobe church, finished in 1791, still stands.

title: Yerba Buena Begins
description: William A. Richardson builds a homestead by the anchorage at Yerba Buena Cove and, with Alcalde Francisco de Haro, lays out a street plan.

title: The Stars and Stripes
description: Capt. John B. Montgomery of USS Portsmouth lands a party of sailors and marines and raises the U.S. flag at the plaza soon named Portsmouth Square.

title: Yerba Buena Renamed
description: Lt. Washington Bartlett's proclamation changing the name Yerba Buena to San Francisco takes effect.

title: Gold!
description: James W. Marshall finds gold at Sutter's Mill in Coloma, setting off the California gold rush that turns the village by Yerba Buena Cove into an instant city.

title: Golden Gate Park
description: Golden Gate Park is established; engineer William Hammond Hall surveys the site that year.

title: First Cable Car
description: Andrew Hallidie's Clay Street Hill Railroad makes its inaugural run on Clay Street between Kearny and Jones; regular service starts September 1.

title: Ferry Building Opens
description: A. Page Brown's Beaux-Arts Ferry Building opens at the foot of Market Street, replacing an 1875 wooden depot.

title: The Great Earthquake
description: A magnitude 7.9 earthquake strikes at 5:12 a.m.; fires burn for four days and more than 80% of the city is destroyed.

title: Muni Begins
description: The city-owned Municipal Railway starts service with a streetcar line on Geary Street.

title: Panama-Pacific Exposition
description: The world's fair opens on a 636-acre site between the Presidio and Fort Mason, today's Marina District; the Palace of Fine Arts survives.

title: Berkeley Fire
description: A wind-driven fire out of Wildcat Canyon consumes some 640 structures, 584 of them houses, in the neighborhoods north of the University of California campus in a single afternoon.

title: Coit Tower
description: Coit Tower, built with Lillie Hitchcock Coit's bequest to Arthur Brown Jr.'s design, is dedicated atop Telegraph Hill.

title: Alcatraz Penitentiary
description: The federal penitentiary on Alcatraz Island opens; it closes in 1963.

title: Bay Bridge Opens
description: The San Francisco–Oakland Bay Bridge opens, six months before the Golden Gate Bridge.

title: Golden Gate Bridge Opens
description: The Golden Gate Bridge opens to the public.

title: Treasure Island Fair
description: The Golden Gate International Exposition opens on Treasure Island, an artificial island built for the fair beside Yerba Buena Island.

title: UN Charter Signed
description: Delegates from 50 Allied nations sign the United Nations Charter in the Veterans Building at Civic Center.

title: Embarcadero Freeway
description: The first section of the double-deck Embarcadero Freeway opens along the waterfront; that January the supervisors' freeway revolt had blocked further routes.

title: Human Be-In
description: An estimated 20,000–30,000 people gather at the Golden Gate Park Polo Fields, a prelude to the Summer of Love.

title: Occupation of Alcatraz
description: 89 American Indians and supporters begin a 19-month occupation of Alcatraz Island.

title: Transamerica Pyramid
description: The 853-ft pyramid is completed on the former site of the Montgomery Block; it stays the city's tallest building until 2017.

title: BART Under the Bay
description: The Transbay Tube opens to BART service, the last segment of the original system.

title: Moscone and Milk Killed
description: Mayor George Moscone and Supervisor Harvey Milk are shot and killed in City Hall by former supervisor Dan White.

title: Loma Prieta Earthquake
description: A magnitude 6.9 quake strikes at 5:04 p.m.; Marina District buildings burn and collapse and a Bay Bridge deck section falls.

title: The Freeway Comes Down
description: Demolition of the quake-damaged Embarcadero Freeway begins, reopening the waterfront in front of the Ferry Building.

title: Oakland Hills Firestorm
description: A wind-driven fire above the Caldecott Tunnel burns 1,520 acres of the Oakland and Berkeley hills; 25 people die and 2,843 houses and 437 apartment and condominium units are destroyed.

title: Pac Bell Park Opens
description: The Giants' ballpark (now Oracle Park) opens at China Basin, the first MLB park built without public funds since 1962.

title: New Bay Bridge Span
description: The new eastern span, with its self-anchored suspension bridge, opens on Labor Day, replacing the quake-damaged original.

title: North Bay Firestorm
description: The Tubbs Fire, started near Calistoga the evening before, runs into Santa Rosa overnight: more than 5,600 structures burn - Coffey Park and Fountaingrove among them - and 22 people die; 44 are killed across the region's October fires.

title: Atlas Fire
description: Begun the same night near Atlas Peak Road, the Atlas Fire burns 51,624 acres between Lake Berryessa and Napa, destroys 783 structures and kills six.

title: Salesforce Transit Center
description: The new transit center and its rooftop park open beside Salesforce Tower, the city's tallest building, which opened in January.

title: Kincade Fire
description: Starting at The Geysers at 9:24 p.m., the Kincade Fire burns 77,758 acres of northern Sonoma County in two weeks; Geyserville, Healdsburg and Windsor are evacuated and CAL FIRE inspectors count 374 destroyed structures.

title: Shelter in Place
description: A joint order by seven Bay Area health departments takes effect, closing non-essential business - among the first COVID-19 measures in the U.S.

title: CZU Lightning Complex
description: Lightning fires of August 16 in the Santa Cruz Mountains merge in a wind shift two days later; they destroy 1,490 buildings in and around Boulder Creek, Bonny Doon and Swanton.

title: LNU Lightning Complex
description: Lightning fires merge into the Hennessey Fire in the hills between Napa, Fairfield and Vacaville; the complex burns 363,220 acres in five counties, destroys 1,491 structures and kills six.

title: Glass Fire
description: Starting at 3:48 a.m. near Deer Park, the Glass Fire burns 67,484 acres and destroys 1,555 structures - 308 homes and 343 commercial buildings in Napa County, 334 homes in Sonoma County.
